content.text: Definition of and – Learner’s Dictionary andconjunction uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio strong /ænd/ weak /ənd, ən/ us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio and conjunction (JOIN) Add to word list Add to word list A1 used to join two words or two parts of a sentence: tea and coffee We were tired and hungry. Tim lives in Brighton and Anne in Oxford. She was my little sister and I looked after her. the kings and queens of Englanda knife and fork and conjunction (AFTER) A1 used to say that one thing happens after another thing: I got dressed and had my breakfast. She leaned forward and whispered in my ear. He got out of his car and ran towards the house. and conjunction (SO) so: The car wouldn't start and I had to get a taxi. and conjunction (AFTER VERB) A2 used instead of 'to' after some verbs, such as 'try' and 'go': Try and eat something. and conjunction (NUMBERS) A1 used when saying or adding numbers: It cost a hundred and twenty pounds. Two and three equals five. and conjunction (EMPHASIZE) B1 used between two words that are the same to make their meaning stronger: The sound grew louder and louder.
